chapter: Big bands, small groups and studio work
title: Trio at the Onyx while on the CBS staff

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Let's see, we talked about your being on staff at CBS, and we kind of eased into Carmen Jones. Let's fill in a couple of gaps in between those. It says in Chalton's book that when you were on CBS staff you also had a trio at the Onyx Club.
Oh yes. That's what I was telling you before, Bill, when Frank Sinatra came down to see me. Well I had

a trio, the hours at CBS weren't bad, we used to do that Good Morning Blues program, we were out of there at 3:00 in the afternoon, and we were through until the next morning at 8:00. Now of course during that time from 8 till 3, we had a lot of time in between. Do the Good Morning Blues program and maybe rehearse an hour after that. We were through about 10:30, 11:00. We were off then until about one, come back and rehearse Perry Como and Dorothy Collins and we were through until the next morning. So we didn't have too much to play during that time, just wire brushes and little things, there playing behind Perry Como and Dorothy, and...

No, so then you wanted to play something, so at the time there was Johnny Guarnieri playing with Raymond and Hank D'Amico. So I got both of them, we formed this little trio, I did, and they wanted a trio in the Onyx Club and we said we'd take it, and we'd go to work late, I think another band was in there, Hot Lips Paige or somebody, and I told the manager, we could come to work early, say 9:00, but could we get off at one, because we had an early show to do in the morning at CBS, and he said okay, and we'd come to work at 9, the other band wouldn't come to work until about 10:30, they had to work till 2:30 or 3:00.
So there was always music happening. When a band was on break then the other was playing.

That's right. That's right, and then by the band that came in late were off late, they'd get home around 4:00, whereas it would be a little too late for us to get home at that time, to get up 7:00 to make our gig at CBS. So, we did that and it gave us a chance to stretch out and play. Frank Sinatra came in there one time, he got in a fight, somebody standing in front of him and I think he punched him in the mouth. I've got a write-up somewhere in my scrapbook there. And we worked there oh, in the Onyx Club I'd say six or eight months.
Did that end when you went with Carmen Jones?
Oh yeah, yeah, 'cause Carmen Jones was well, it was legit theatre, Wednesday matinee and a Saturday matinee and that ended then, yeah.
